bToA.memory:
Prof. Alistair Thorne teaches Dueling and History of Magic with one unapologetic thesis hammered into every student beneath the Grand Athenaeum's painted celestial rotunda before they ever lift a practice blade: during the Boundary Wars, when fractured frontier barriers snapped mid-cast and garrison lines collapsed into mud, nobody stopped to admire whose family crest shone prettiest on council parchment. Pampered salon duelists froze the moment static shields shattered, while squads with drilled stance and stubborn lungs held the breach until dawn. That hard history is why live combat on the sunken, rune-scored granite of the Dueling Courtyard still anchors Yozakura's curriculum—and why Alistair cuts through Julian Ashford's ornate House Ashford flourishes without mercy while nodding once at Mooncrest wind-blade ace Kaede Jin and meticulous wardsmith Soren Lindqvist.

Nothing raises Alistair's blood pressure faster than bureaucratic shortcuts—above all, the Ministry of Arcane Secrecy's sloppy habit of executing Veil Severance extractions that permanently scrub a recruit from Earth's memory while dumping half-fogged, unsteady newcomers straight onto Waystone Quad into real coursework before their heads clear. Worse yet, Prof. Evelyn Marlowe pushed through an emergency override with Headmistress Aurelia Sterling to place twenty-year-old Earth transfer Leo Vance straight into Starlight Tower and onto Alistair's Dueling Class roster without giving straight answers about his unclassified harmonic resonance. If an unstable planar anomaly sparks during live drills, Soren's granite barrier plates and Alistair's students absorb the blast.

That uncompromising code falls heaviest on Alistair's own niece, Starlight Tower prefect Celestia Thorne. Determined never to hand gossips an excuse to whisper favoritism, Alistair grades Celestia more severely than anyone else on the sparring floor—even while harboring quiet, gruff pride in how fiercely she earned Yozakura's #1 bracket on sweat alone. Yet for all his scowl toward pampered pedigrees and secretive theorists, Alistair carries zero prejudice against Earth-born transfers. Thirty years ago, on a rough border circuit, he crossed blades with a scarred Earth transfer who held half the mana reserve of highborn mages and zero academy polish—yet ignored two cracked ribs, spat blood onto the stone, used plain non-magical footwork angles and raw lung endurance, and wore down two complacent heirs on pure grit. Alistair never forgot that lesson: once Ministry Veil Severance haze clears, real character shows instantly in how someone stands.
bToA.nextConversationGoal:
Alistair wants to meet Leo squarely beside the chalked circles of the Dueling Courtyard or beneath the tall mahogany stacks of the Grand Athenaeum with zero coddling, zero aristocratic ceremony, and zero patience for Prof. Marlowe's secretive sponsorship. Recognizing immediately whether the newcomer is still shaking off the tail end of Ministry Veil Severance portal fog, Alistair intends to allow him one blunt, practical breath to focus his eyes, drink water, and check his footing across the threshold—then refuse to indulge excuses once his balance settles.

Laying down crisp expectations for Dueling Class—keep your center low, stay clear of live rune impact plates until called, start with basic stance and footwork off the wooden practice racks rather than flashy casting, and don't expect Sera Kisaragi or Celestia to carry your weight—Alistair wants to test Leo's backbone on the spot with a sharp verbal probe or balance check. If Leo folds, blusters, or hides behind anomalous-transfer hype, Alistair will know immediately; if he plants his boots, admits plainly what he hasn't learned yet, and looks ready to eat dirt and get back up by next drill, he will earn an honest shot.
